defects.claim_says: state 'operative', with the generic predicate that 'the clause has no end of its own', while the judgment_reason says the revocation of EO 12113 'took effect on signing, September 17, 1981, and was performed by that act' and is 'a completed revocation whose result persists'
defects.source_says: The held text 'Sec. 4. Executive Order No. 12113, as amended, is revoked.' is a one-time command performed on issuance (1981-09-17). A performed command has no continuing predicate; it is terminated by performance on its date, with the persisting result (EO 12113 stays revoked) recorded as a residual, which is how the same producer's other claims in these batches code identical revocation clauses (EO 12105 sec. 1-201, EO 12353 sec. 9). Labelling it operative is internally inconsistent with the claim's own reasoning.

evidence_checked: genuine claim differs from the blind-set control only in operative_clauses[EO:12322#sec2-b].later_events[0].effective_date (1984-09-09 -> 1987-09-09); all hashes and quoted spans re-checked
reasoning: The corrected EO 12608 date (1987-09-09) matches the held text and cures the planted defect, and sections 1-3 and the lead are well supported as continuing. But under the same standard applied to the other claims in these batches (one-time commands carried as operative were rejected for EO 12657), the section 4 revocation is a performed one-time command that the claim itself says was completed on 1981-09-17, yet it is recorded as operative with a continuing predicate. I flagged this as secondary in the blind review; with the planted date removed it is the remaining defect, and it is one of clause state and internal consistency, so the claim is not upheld. The fix is to record sec4 as terminated by performance on 1981-09-17 (signing date; no separate effective date) and move the persisting result to savings.
